children: Bank of America is standing by CoreWeave
after a sharp two-day selloff, arguing that the AI infrastructure company's growth outlook remains strong enough to justify a premium valuation despite mounting concerns over financing.
The bank kept its
Buy rating and $140 price target
on CoreWeave after the stock fell roughly
18% over two sessions
Analyst Tal Liani said the decline likely reflected investor concerns around the increasingly difficult financing environment for AI infrastructure companies.
Still, BofA actually raised its revenue expectations.
The firm now forecasts CoreWeave revenue of
$26.5 billion in 2027
and
$43.3 billion in 2028
, up from previous estimates of $26 billion and $41 billion.
That would represent growth of roughly
BofA expects CoreWeave to add about
1.4 to 1.5 gigawatts of active power capacity annually
over the next two years. Revenue per megawatt could also increase to around $14 by the end of 2028 from roughly $10 today as the company deploys Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips.
But the expansion comes at an enormous cost.
BofA raised its spending forecasts to
$47.4 billion in 2027 and $49.8 billion in 2028
The bank estimates CoreWeave could spend about
$23.8 billion more cash than it generates in 2026
and another $24.8 billion in 2027.
Investor Takeaway
I think this call highlights the central contradiction in the CoreWeave story.
The company's growth outlook is extraordinary, but so are its financing requirements.
CoreWeave has at least
$129 billion in contracted backlog

, supported largely by major technology customers. Meta accounts for $35 billion and OpenAI another $22.4 billion, while Microsoft's share of backlog has fallen materially, improving customer diversification.
That backlog gives lenders visibility and may help CoreWeave finance expansion.
But investors still have to decide whether enough value remains for equity holders after the debt and capital spending required to build all that capacity.
For investors, the key things to watch are
borrowing costs, free cash flow, power capacity additions, revenue per megawatt and whether the backlog continues translating into profitable growth
BofA clearly believes the answer is yes. The market is becoming much less certain.

title: Bank of America Has Blunt Message on CoreWeave Stock After Selloff
